{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Eldon Robert Hansen''' (born 1927) is an American mathematician and author who has published in global optimization theory and [[interval arithmetic]].

Hansen was born on July 16, 1927 in [[Rochester, Washington]]. After receiving bachelor's and master's degrees at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1950 and 1952, and working at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|University of California Radiation Laboratory]] from 1952 until 1956,<ref name=abio>Author biography from {{cite journal
 | last1 = Huynen | first1 = J.
 | last2 = McNolty | first2 = Frank
 | last3 = Hansen | first3 = Eldon
 | date = November 1975
 | doi = 10.1109/taes.1975.308189
 | issue = 6
 | journal = IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
 | pages = 1316–1332
 | title = Component Distributions for Fluctuating Radar Targets
 | volume = AES-11}}</ref> he received his Ph.D. in mathematics from [[Stanford University]] in 1960 with a dissertation on [[Jacobi method]]s and Block-Jacobi methods for computing [[Eigenvalue algorithm|matrix eigenvalues]], supervised by [[George Forsythe]].<ref name=mg>{{mathgenealogy|25013}}</ref> He worked for the [[Lockheed Missiles and Space Company]] beginning in 1956.<ref name=abio/>
He later held a position at [[Washington State University]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37302092300|title=Eldon Hansen|work=IEEE Xplore|publisher=IEEE|access-date=March 15, 2025}}</ref> and supervised a doctoral student there.<ref name=mg/>

His books include:
*''Global Optimization Using Interval Analysis'' (Marcel Dekker, 1992; 2nd ed. with William G. Walster, 2004)<ref>Reviews of ''Global Optimization Using Interval Analysis'': M. Krastanov, {{MR|1197883}}; John J. Dinkel, {{zbl|0762.90069}}; Günter Mayer, {{zbl|1103.90092}}</ref>
*''A Table of Series and Products'' (Prentice-Hall, 1975)<ref>Review of ''A Table of Series and Products'': L. Carlitz, {{zbl|0438.00001}}</ref>
*''Topics in Interval Analysis'' (edited, Clarendon Press, 1969)<ref>Review of ''Topics in Interval Analysis'': D. Kershaw, ''Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society'', {{doi|10.1017/S0013091500009287}}</ref>
